tagline: Commercial landscape maintenance across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach — since 1984

why_choose_us.title: Forty-two years on South Florida properties
why_choose_us.description: GreenTree has maintained commercial grounds here since 1984. In a trade where service quietly decays after the first ninety days, four decades of renewed contracts is the only proof that actually means anything.

why_choose_us.title: Maintenance is the whole business, not the side business
why_choose_us.description: Most landscape companies treat maintenance as what the crews do between installations. It is the only thing GreenTree has done since 1984 — which is why the schedule holds and the details do not slip.

why_choose_us.title: Family owned and run — no rotating account manager
why_choose_us.description: The trade is consolidating fast, and buyers keep watching the local company they hired turn into a regional brand with a call centre. GreenTree is still independent, still family run, and the people answering are the people responsible.

why_choose_us.title: A Minority Certified vendor your procurement team can approve
why_choose_us.description: If your organisation carries supplier-diversity requirements, GreenTree meets them without asking you to trade down on quality — a certification most commercial landscape contractors in South Florida cannot offer.

gallery.title: Scheduled mowing on a commercial site
gallery.alt: Crew member in a high-visibility vest mowing a commercial lawn on a zero-turn mower beside a glass office building
gallery.description: Grounds run on a fixed schedule, so your team knows exactly when the property is serviced.

gallery.title: Beds and turf held to one standard
gallery.alt: Manicured commercial lawn with curved planting beds, mixed shrubs and seasonal colour
gallery.description: Clean bed edges and weed-free borders are what a visitor reads as a well-run property.

gallery.title: Mature trees and open lawn
gallery.alt: Broad open lawn framed by mature shade trees and dense shrub borders
gallery.description: Large open turf and mature plantings need different attention in the same visit — that is what a maintenance-only crew is built for.

gallery.title: Irrigation checked on a cycle
gallery.alt: Irrigation head spraying water in an arc across a green lawn
gallery.description: Heads, arcs and coverage inspected on schedule, so a fault is found before the turf shows it.

gallery.title: Pruning cut to the plant, not the calendar
gallery.alt: Hand pruners making a clean cut on a rose cane above an outward-facing bud
gallery.description: Cutting to the growth habit is what keeps the shape between visits instead of forcing a hard cutback later.

gallery.title: Seasonal colour at the entrance
gallery.alt: Close-up of an apricot-coloured rose in full bloom against dark foliage
gallery.description: Entrance plantings are the first thing a tenant, client or inspector sees.

gallery.title: Defined edges through common areas
gallery.alt: Curving lawn path bordered by dense red and white flower beds
gallery.description: Edging is the cheapest thing on a maintenance contract and the first thing anyone notices when it stops happening.

gallery.title: Formal beds kept in shape
gallery.alt: Formal garden with symmetrical planting beds, clipped borders and a central fountain
gallery.description: Structured plantings need a crew that returns on the same cycle — not one that visits when someone complains.

services_section.subtitle: Maintenance, pruning, irrigation and planting for commercial properties across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach Counties — one company, one crew, one scope.

closing_cta.headline: Ask us for a proposal on your property
closing_cta.body: GreenTree has maintained commercial grounds across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach Counties since 1984 — family owned, Minority Certified, and dedicated solely to landscape maintenance.

blog_section.heading: Grounds Management Notes
blog_section.description: Practical guidance for South Florida property managers, HOA boards and facility teams on turf, irrigation, pruning cycles and what a maintenance contract should actually cover.
